title: Relative Frobenius
statement: Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $q=p^a$ and $k$ the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0=\mathbf F_q$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be its geometric base change, where $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $\Phi_X,\Phi_Y$ be the base changes of the absolute $q$-power Frobenii on the models, as in [d-relative-frob]. For every integer $m\geq1$, form $X'_m=Y\times_{\Phi_Y^m,Y,f}X$ and let $r_m=(f,\Phi_X^m):X\to X'_m$ be the unique map with first projection $f$ and second projection $\Phi_X^m$, as in [d-relative-frob]. Then $r_m$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and is a universal homeomorphism, meaning that every base change is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism, sk-d-setup].

proof.text: Fix $m\geq1$ and put $Q=q^m=p^{am}$. Write $H=F_{X_0/Y_0}:X_0\to Z_0=Y_0\times_{F_{Y_0},Y_0,f_0}X_0$ for the relative $Q$-power Frobenius, and $\pi:Z_0\to X_0$ for the second projection. The definition gives $\pi H=F_{X_0}$ and identifies $r_m$ with $H\times_{k_0}\operatorname{id}_k$. Here $F_{X_0}$ and $F_{Y_0}$ denote absolute $Q$-power Frobenii, whereas the maps on $X,Y$ in the item are their model base changes. We prove the two properties of $H$ and then extend scalars.

source.place: Proof, opening paragraph; current main-20261015 statement with d-relative-frob

proof.text: The structure map $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is of finite type and $Y_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is separated. Apply the finite-type-to-separated-target statement to this commutative triangle to see that $f_0$ is of finite type, hence locally of finite type. Choose affine opens $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ covering $Y_0$ and affine opens $V_{ij}=\operatorname{Spec}S_{ij}$ covering $f_0^{-1}(U_i)$ with $S_{ij}$ a finitely generated $R_i$-algebra, as the definition of local finite type allows.

source.place: Proof, Step 1: choice of finitely generated affine coordinate algebras; finite-type hypothesis made explicit

proof.text: On such a pair $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}S$, the corresponding affine open $W\subset Z_0$ has ring $B=R\otimes_{F,R}S$ and the map of $H$ is $h:B\to S$, $r'\otimes s\mapsto g(r')s^Q$, where $g:R\to S$ is the map of $f_0$. Its image contains $g(R)$, since $h(r'\otimes1)=g(r')$, and all $Q$-th powers, since $h(1\otimes s)=s^Q$. Choose algebra generators $s_1,\ldots,s_n$. For each monomial $s^e$ write $e_i=Qa_i+b_i$, $0\leq b_i<Q$. Then $g(r)s^e=h(r\otimes s^a)s^b$. Every polynomial expression in the generators is therefore a $B$-linear combination of the finitely many $s^b$ with $0\leq b_i<Q$. Thus $S$ is a finite $B$-module. This is generation, not a claim of independence or freeness.

source.place: Proof, Step 1, monomial argument; compare Stacks varieties.tex Tag 0CCD, lemma-relative-frobenius-finite

proof.text: The opens $W_{ij}$ above cover $Z_0$: for a point $z$, choose $i$ containing its $Y_0$-projection and $j$ containing its $X_0$-projection. This is possible because $F_{Y_0}$ is the identity on points and $F_{Y_0}\operatorname{pr}_1=f_0\pi$. Moreover $H^{-1}(W_{ij})=f_0^{-1}(U_i)\cap F_{X_0}^{-1}(V_{ij})=V_{ij}$, since $F_{X_0}$ is the identity on points and $V_{ij}\subseteq f_0^{-1}(U_i)$. The affine descriptions and these inverse images are those of d-relative-frob. The finite-local-on-target criterion, condition (2), applied to the finite ring maps in step 3, proves $H$ finite. A finite morphism is integral, so $H$ is integral as well.

source.place: Tag 01WI, lemma-finite-local, (2) implies (1); Tag 01WJ, lemma-finite-integral; affine opens as in the blueprint Step 1

proof.text: For either $T=X_0$ or $T=Y_0$, the absolute $q$-power Frobenius $A_T$ is a universal homeomorphism by the absolute finite-field Frobenius statement; it has no finite-type hypothesis. Its $m$-th iterate is $F_T$, since repeated powers on sections give $s\mapsto s^{q^m}$ and the underlying map stays the identity. To verify the universal property for the iterate explicitly, fix $T'\to T$. The pullback of $A_T^{j+1}=A_T\circ A_T^j$ factors through $T\times_{A_T,T}T'$: the second arrow is a pullback of $A_T$, and the first is a pullback of $A_T^j$. These identifications follow by matching the two projections of the fibre products. For $j=0$ the base change is the identity; induction makes each of the two arrows a homeomorphism, so their composite is a homeomorphism. This proves every base change of $F_T$ is a homeomorphism, exactly the definition. The field $k_0$ continues to have $q$ elements throughout this induction.

source.place: Tag 0CC8, lemma-frobenius, with the q-power theorem iterated; pullback factorization expanded from the universal property

proof.text: Since $\pi$ is the base change of $F_{Y_0}$ along $f_0$, it is a universal homeomorphism. In particular its underlying map is injective, by taking the identity base change in the definition. To prove $H$ surjective, let $z\in Z_0$. Since $F_{X_0}$ is the identity on points, take $x=\pi(z)\in X_0$. Then $\pi(H(x))=F_{X_0}(x)=\pi(z)$; injectivity of $\pi$ gives $H(x)=z$.

source.place: Proof, Step 2 final sentence and Step 3 surjectivity argument; Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 0CEU, lemma-base-change-universal-homeomorphism

proof.text: Every base change of $F_{X_0}$ is a homeomorphism by step 5, hence is injective; thus $F_{X_0}$ is universally injective by the definition in the radicial-morphism node. The field-point equivalence in that node now says that $F_{X_0}$ is injective on $K$-valued points for every field $K$. If $u,v:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X_0$ satisfy $Hu=Hv$, composing with $\pi$ gives $F_{X_0}u=F_{X_0}v$, hence $u=v$. Apply the same field-point equivalence in the reverse direction to conclude that $H$ is universally injective. Along with integrality from step 4 and surjectivity from step 6, the integral-radicial-surjective criterion proves that $H$ is a universal homeomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01S4, lemma-universally-injective, field-point equivalence; Tag 04DF, lemma-universal-homeomorphism, (2) implies (1); blueprint Step 3

proof.text: Finally, finite morphisms are preserved by arbitrary base change, as are universal homeomorphisms. Apply the two cited permanence statements to $H$ along $k_0\to k$. Under the canonical identification of d-relative-frob, its base change is precisely $r_m$, so $r_m$ is finite and a universal homeomorphism for the chosen $m\geq1$.
